headline_marked: Over 5 lakh fail as [[HSC pass rate hits 22-year low]]
headline: Over 5 lakh fail as HSC pass rate hits 22-year low
summary: The pass rate for this year's Higher Secondary Certificate exams dropped to 51.62%, the lowest since 2004.
details: The pass rate in this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examinations fell to a 22-year low, with more than five lakh students failing under the nine general education boards.
The pass rate stood at 51.62 percent, down from 57.12 percent last year, according to results published on Saturday.
An analysis of historical data from the BANBEIS shows that the last time the pass rate was lower than this year was in 2004, when it stood at 47.73 percent.
Across all 11 education boards, including the Madrasa and Technical education boards, 5,94,113 students failed, up from 5,08,701 last year.
The combined pass rate across all 11 boards stood at 52.12 percent, compared with 58.83 percent in 2025.
The number of students securing GPA-5, the highest grade, also fell to an eight-year low, with only 40,084 students achieving the top grade across all 11 boards.
Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon acknowledged that the overall results were unsatisfactory and stated that the government would take steps to address students' learning gaps.
caption:
Over 5 lakh students failed their HSC exams this year, marking a 22-year low in pass rates.

The pass rate in this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examinations fell to a 22-year low, with more than five lakh students failing under the nine general education boards.

The pass rate stood at 51.62 percent, down from 57.12 percent last year, according to results published on Saturday.

An analysis of historical data from the BANBEIS shows that the last time the pass rate was lower than this year was in 2004, when it stood at 47.73 percent.

Across all 11 education boards, including the Madrasa and Technical education boards, 5,94,113 students failed, up from 5,08,701 last year.

The combined pass rate across all 11 boards stood at 52.12 percent, compared with 58.83 percent in 2025.

The number of students securing GPA-5, the highest grade, also fell to an eight-year low, with only 40,084 students achieving the top grade across all 11 boards.

Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon acknowledged that the overall results were unsatisfactory and stated that the government would take steps to address students' learning gaps.

headline: Video of Hasina's exit suspected motive in former Air Force officer's murder
summary: Police suspect Tahsif Souri may have been killed for recording and circulating a video of ousted PM Sheikh Hasina leaving Bangladesh.
details: Former Air Force officer Tahsif Souri's body was recovered from the Turag River near Rajabari Ghat on Wednesday. His father has since filed a murder case following the discovery.
caption:
A former Air Force officer may have been killed for sharing a video of ousted PM Sheikh Hasina's departure from Bangladesh.

Former Air Force officer Tahsif Souri's body was recovered from the Turag River near Rajabari Ghat on Wednesday. His father has since filed a murder case following the discovery.
